business.text: Adobe sells subscription software for making and managing digital content: Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere and the rest of Creative Cloud for creators, Acrobat and Express for everyone else, and Experience Cloud for marketing teams. Almost all revenue is recurring subscriptions.

read.headline: Adobe beat and raised full-year fiscal 2026 EPS guidance to $24.35-$24.45 with a Q3 revenue guide above consensus, and the note records the stock being traded on AI-displacement headlines rather than on those numbers, into a September 10 print.

guidance.quote: Management guided fiscal 2026 EPS to $24.35 to $24.45 and Q3 to $6.05 to $6.10, both above consensus

tone.assessment: Confident on the numbers, inferred entirely from guidance behavior rather than from any recorded management language: the company beat, raised the full-year EPS range, and set both the annual and the quarterly guide above consensus — not the posture of a management team bracing the market. The note offers no counterweight from the company's side on the AI question, and pairs this guidance with its own observation that the market is not pricing off it.
tone.evidence: Management guided fiscal 2026 EPS to $24.35 to $24.45 and Q3 to $6.05 to $6.10, both above consensus
tone.confidence: low — the note contains no earnings call transcript, no prepared remarks, no management quotes and no Q&A. Tone is being read off guidance numbers alone, which shows what management committed to but not how they sounded, what they hedged, or what they were pressed on.

dodged.topic: Digital Media ARR and net new ARR — the metric the note's own thesis killers are written in
dodged.reasoning: The note defines its kill criteria in ARR terms ('Digital Media ARR growth falling under 8%, two consecutive quarters of net new ARR decline') and asserts in the bear case that 'Net new ARR has decelerated.', yet no ARR number appears anywhere in the file: no growth rate, no dollar figure, no quarter count. The 'Last two earnings reports' section carries only the beat statement, the FY guide raise, the Q3 revenue guide, the September 10 date and three analyst actions. The one disclosure that would settle the note's own tests is missing from the section where it belongs. Whether management dodged it on the call or the note simply did not record it cannot be told from this file.

dodged.topic: CEO succession — no successor, timeline, or reason
dodged.reasoning: The note twice treats the CEO exit as material ('The CEO is leaving, which is a real management question mark.'; 'The CEO exit removes the person who built the subscription transition.') and makes 'a poorly received CEO appointment' a thesis killer, yet supplies no name, no departure date, no stated reason and no search status. A risk weighted that heavily with zero surrounding detail is either thinly addressed by the company or thinly captured here.

'a cut to fiscal 2027 guidance below fiscal 2026' is listed as a thesis killer, but the file contains no FY2027 guidance, framework, or management comment of any kind — guidance in the note stops at the FY2026 range and the Q3 guide. The test cannot be run against anything in this file.

dodged.topic: Any direct response to the AI-displacement case
dodged.reasoning: The bear case is entirely about generative tools and pricing model ('Per seat pricing is the wrong model for an agent era, so even if Adobe wins on product the pricing shrinks.'), and the note says the market 'has ignored the numbers and traded on AI headlines'. Against that, the file records no management rebuttal, no AI-attributed revenue, no pricing change, and no Firefly monetization figure — Firefly appears only inside the 850 million MAU count. Since the note contains no call content at all, I can observe the absence but cannot attribute it to management.

thesis.why_on_the_list: Compounder bucket. Rank 4 of 150 on quality (ROIC 31% average, 39% of revenue turns into free cash, share count down 9% over the window) while the stock is 59% below its all time high and trades near 10 to 12 times forward earnings against a four year median of 38. This is the cheapest a business of this quality has been in the data.
thesis.business_quality: Moat is the file formats, the training and habits of every professional creative, and Acrobat as the default for PDFs. Management guided fiscal 2026 EPS to $24.35 to $24.45 and Q3 to $6.05 to $6.10, both above consensus, and ran a $25 billion buyback. Monthly active users across Acrobat, Creative Cloud, Express and Firefly reached 850 million, up 17% year over year. The CEO is leaving, which is a real management question mark. Insider ownership is small (0.2%).
thesis.verdict: Buy, but after the September 10 report rather than before it. The print will either confirm the numbers or give a better price. Buy zone $250 to $300. Conviction 4 of 5.
thesis.action: Buy, but after the September 10 report rather than before it

logged.thesis: Rank 4 on quality, about 12x guided fiscal 2026 EPS, 59% off the high, $25 billion buyback, MAUs up 17%. The AI bear case has not shown up in the numbers yet.
logged.wrong_if: Digital Media ARR growth under 8%, net new ARR down twice, or a close under $220.

risks.bear_case: Generative image and video tools from OpenAI, Midjourney, Runway and Canva do 80% of what a prosumer needs for free or nearly free, and design tools inside AI chat products (Anthropic's Claude Design launched in April) push more of that base away every quarter. Per seat pricing is the wrong model for an agent era, so even if Adobe wins on product the pricing shrinks. Net new ARR has decelerated. The CEO exit removes the person who built the subscription transition. Cheap can stay cheap for years while the market waits for proof, and a 10x multiple on a business with real terminal value doubt is not obviously a floor.
killers: Digital Media ARR growth falling under 8%, two consecutive quarters of net new ARR decline, a cut to fiscal 2027 guidance below fiscal 2026, or a poorly received CEO appointment

wrong_if.text: Digital Media ARR growth under 8%, net new ARR down twice, or a close under $220.

multiples.label: Forward P/E
multiples.basis_note: The two sides are not the same multiple. The left is a forward P/E, the Street's estimate of next year's earnings. The median on the right is trailing: the price at each fiscal year end divided by that year's reported diluted EPS. Where earnings are expected to grow, forward is mechanically lower than trailing, so this column reads cheap by construction.

multiples.label: EV/EBITDA
multiples.basis_note: Both sides are trailing, so this comparison is like for like.

own_history.caveat: The median is taken at 4 fiscal year ends, so it is a 4-point median. That is a thin basis for 'cheap against its own history' and it says nothing about whether the old multiple was deserved.
own_history.basis_warning: Read the P/E row with care. Across the 136 names that carry both comparisons, 85% print a negative 'vs median' on forward P/E with a median of -29%, against 50% and 0.0% on EV/EBITDA where both sides are trailing. That gap is the basis mismatch, not 136 companies being cheap. It is also correlated with growth: faster-growing names look cheaper here (rank correlation -0.28 against revenue CAGR, versus -0.15 for EV/EBITDA), because their forward earnings are further above their trailing ones. The score weights the like-for-like EV/EBITDA comparison more heavily for exactly this reason.

drawdown.caveat: The all-time high is the highest closing price; the 52-week high is an intraday high. They are not on the same basis, and the drawdown from the all-time high is therefore understated.

price_basis.note: The drawdowns and the multiple-versus-median above were computed inside the price screen from its own last close, which is not quite the price shown at the top of this page: the two come from different passes of the pipeline and differ by a fraction of a percent. Neither is wrong; they are just not the same number.

peer_set.caveat: Compared against 16 other names in Software - Application.

peers.verdict: cheap against peers of better quality
peers.reasoning: It sits in the cheaper end of its peer set while its measured quality sits in the better end. That is the combination worth a closer look, and it is also the combination most often explained by something the numbers do not carry: a customer loss, a patent cliff, a regulator. The gap is a question, not an answer.
peers.why: The own-history comparison above says nothing about whether the old multiple was deserved. This asks a different question: where does this name sit among its peers on price, and where does it sit among them on the things a price is supposed to reflect.

written_view.text: At $285.75 with fiscal 2026 EPS guidance of about $24.40, the stock is about 11.7 times this year's earnings. Six month revenue to May 29, 2026 was $13.0 billion with $4.66 billion of operating income and $8.86 of diluted EPS; the company bought back $4.6 billion of stock in those six months. Cash $4.9 billion, debt $6.6 billion. Peers: Autodesk 16.7x forward, Microsoft 21.6x, ServiceNow 29x, Salesforce not in our universe screen. Three year view at $24.40 growing 8% a year gives roughly $30 to $31 of EPS in fiscal 2029. Bear: 10x on $27 (growth stalls, seat losses) is $270, roughly flat. Base: 15x on $30 is $450. Bull: 20x on $32 is $640. The asymmetry is what makes it a pick, not certainty about AI.

score.caveat: A percentile against 150 names on one date. It has not been backtested; see the positioning page for why not.
